claude_proposed_widenings.name: AnchorTarget { kind: "self" }
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Contingency's anchor is the caster themselves, not a location or area. AnchorTarget currently only has 'location' and 'area' variants.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: The contingent spell takes effect only on you

claude_proposed_widenings.name: AnchoredEvent { kind: "player_described_condition"; description: string }
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Contingency's trigger is an arbitrary free-form condition described by the player at cast time. The current AnchoredEvent closed enum (physical_contact, enters_area) cannot represent open-ended trigger conditions. This is a genuine structural gap: the condition predicate is not a deterministic engine-evaluable formula but a natural-language description adjudicated at runtime.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: The contingent spell takes effect when a certain trigger occurs. You describe that trigger when you cast the two spells. For example, a Contingency cast with Water Breathing might stipulate that Water Breathing comes into effect when you are engulfed in water or a similar liquid.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: AnchoredSignal { kind: "stored_spell_release" }
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The signal emitted when the trigger fires is 'release the stored contingent spell on the caster'. AnchoredSignal only has 'audible' and 'mental'. The stored spell is the payload, not a notification signal.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: The contingent spell takes effect immediately after the trigger occurs for the first time, whether or not you want it to, and then Contingency ends.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: stored_spell_reference — cast-time constrained spell capture
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Contingency captures a second spell at cast time (constrained to: level ≤5, action casting time, self-targetable). This spell's full payload is held and released on trigger. No existing surface type represents a 'choose a spell at cast time, apply constraint filter, hold payload for deferred release' pattern.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: Choose a spell of level 5 or lower that you can cast, that has a casting time of an action, and that can target you. You cast that spell—called the contingent spell—as part of casting Contingency

claude_proposed_widenings.name: dual_slot_cast — simultaneous dual spell-slot consumption
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Casting Contingency expends two spell slots simultaneously: one L6 slot for Contingency and one L1–5 slot for the contingent spell. The current surface models a single spell_slot resource per cast. No multi-slot consumption pattern exists.
